# Release and CI

Read [`docs/60-release/04-release-pipeline.md`](../../docs/60-release/04-release-pipeline.md) and
[`docs/60-release/01-versioning-and-compatibility.md`](../../docs/60-release/01-versioning-and-compatibility.md)
before editing.

## The one rule that matters most

**Production signing and certification run only on the hardened platform workflows.**
The user-authorized `hosted-release.yml` path publishes explicitly labeled development bundles on
GitHub-hosted runners, without production keys. Target hosts certify and development-sign those
guests before use. See `docs/60-release/07-hosted-development-bundles.md`. Local fixture tests and
compilation do not publish releases.

## CI

`.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs on pull requests and pushes to `main`:

1. restore and build `CSweet.Office.Independent.slnx` with `-p:UseLocalOfficeContracts=false`,
2. `dotnet test tests/CSweet.Office.Tests/CSweet.Office.Tests.csproj`.

The explicit switch is the point of CI: it proves the published package boundary rather than a local Contracts
checkout. Never remove it, and never let a change pass locally only because the sibling repository happens to
exist.

## Version truth

Three values must agree, and only `Get-OfficeReleaseMetadata.ps1` enforces it (the tag must equal
`VersionPrefix`):

| Value | Location |
|---|---|
| Office version | `VersionPrefix` in `Directory.Build.props` |
| Contracts pin | `PackageVersion` for `CSweet.Office.Contracts` in `Directory.Packages.props` |
| Release tag | the git tag `vX.Y.Z` |

When you bump one, check the other two. Office tags are independent of C-Sweet headquarters tags.

## Production release workflow conventions

- Production signing uses manual dispatch; tagged builds default to the hosted development workflow.
- Platform jobs run on the hardened self-hosted runner matrix inside the `production-signing` environment; the
  publish job runs in `production-release`.
- Required inputs come from repository secrets and variables, not from command-line arguments.
- `verify-release.sh` must pass: checksums, JSON validity, SPDX SBOM presence, and a manifest that lists every
  asset.
- The manifest is generated by `New-OfficeReleaseManifest.ps1` from the produced packages; GitHub Releases is
  the canonical immutable asset origin.

## When you change the pipeline

State in the pull request:

1. Which runner labels and environments are affected.
2. Whether any new secret or variable is required, and who must create it.
3. Whether `release/office-release.schema.json` needs to change. If the asset shape changes, the schema change
   is part of the same pull request.
4. Whether `verify-release.sh` still validates everything the pipeline produces.

Never weaken a verification step to make a release succeed. If a check fails, the artifact is wrong.
